page.layout: One page of running text in a single column, with the running head above and a catchword at the lower right. No marginal notes. Reference marks sit inside the text. A stray apostrophe-like mark stands before the second line.

main_text.p: jus esse in ista terrena & temporaria, ut divitias, honores, & æstimationem eam quæ ad mini-ftrum & dispensatorem pertinet, non minus quam in hæcipsa jus est aliis quibuscunq;. Imo magis ista deberi miniftris rerum fpiritualium, docet Apostolus,quàm aliis.Si nos vobis fpitua-lia feminavimus, magnum fuerit, fi nos veftra carnalia meffuerimus? fi alii fui in vos juris par-ticipes funt,cur non potius nos? 1.Cor.9.ɣ[?].11.12. Imo ad Philemonem audacius loquitur: Ut ne dicam,inquit,te etiam teipfum mihi infuper de-bere, Philem.ɣ[?].19. Tantum bonum á miniftris Evangelii fidelibus ad homines redundat,quan-tum nunquam fatis re ulla temporaria & cadu-cà compenfari poteft. In hoc tamen eft fumma miniftri laus, fi Evangelii causâ aliquid de jure fuo remittat. Non usi sumus jure isto, sed omnia sustinemus, ne quid remoremur Evangelium Christi, 1.Cor.9.12. Imo vero id ad omnes Chri-ftianos pertinet, ut potius injuriam patiantur, & damnum accipiant,quàm aliquo modo scan-dalo sint Evangelio Christi, 1.Cor.6.7.

page.notes: The reference marks written "ɣ[?]" in "1.Cor.9.ɣ.11.12." and "Philem.ɣ.19." are an unclear symbol in the printed references; I could not identify it with certainty. The italic "Sed fuimus placidi]" carries a closing bracket as printed; I kept it inside the paragraph. A stray mark sits before "quam in hæcipsa" on the second line; I treated it as a printing speck and did not transcribe it. Spelling is as printed, with long s written as s and u/v and i/j normalised. Words with a printed hyphen at the line end are written with that hyphen.
